fit: isolated oral piperine and evoked pain responses in inflammatory rat models
assessment: The 100 mg/kg treatment increased tolerated paw pressure and reduced evoked vocalizations. The 20 mg/kg group had little vocalization effect. Oral isolated piperine and rodent pain responses give no clinical cracked-pepper estimate.

fit: cold-pressed walnut kernel oil in a mouse demyelinating disease model
assessment: Eight mice per group. Reported disease scores were 2.38 versus 3.00 with saline, with unclear averaging window. The scale rates weakness, paralysis and death. Dystonia and Parkinson disease were not tested.

fit: cold-pressed walnut oil in rotenone-treated cell cultures
assessment: Viability and oxidative measures varied by preparation concentration and time. Cell viability and fly climbing come from separate experiments. Neither measures dystonia after walnut oil consumption.

fit: Parkinson dietary crossover with baseline apathy and no identifiable bell-pepper contrast
assessment: Interviewed participants described pre-existing apathy as a barrier. The trial registered a Starkstein scale, and the report gives baseline prevalence without a post-diet group response and with no assigned roasted bell pepper.

fit: individualized plant-rich timed diet and rated apathy in a Parkinson cohort
assessment: Apathy changed from 13.65 to 9.0 in the diet group and 13.05 to 13.6 in controls. Narrative and tabulated post-treatment comparisons conflict. The intervention did not quantify roasted bell pepper exposure.
